source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_38/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename columns in source1 to avoid collision after join with source0
# But target schema expects 'total_runs' as is, so no rename needed here
# We will join source0 and source1 on 'batsman' and keep total_runs from both sources as separate columns
# To distinguish total_runs columns, rename source1.total_runs to total_runs_1 temporarily
source1_renamed = source1.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_1"})

# Join source0 and source1 on 'batsman' (inner join to keep only batsmen present in both)
df01 = pd.merge(source0, source1_renamed, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Now join df01 with source2 on 'batsman'
df012 = pd.merge(df01, source2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Rename batsman_runs in source2 to batsman_runs_x to match target schema
df012 = df012.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x"})

# Join df012 with source3 on 'batsman'
df_final = pd.merge(df012, source3, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Rename batsman_runs in source3 to batsman_runs_y to match target schema
df_final = df_final.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y"})

# Now the target schema is:
# ['batsman': string, 'batsman_runs_x': float, 'total_runs': integer, 'batsman_runs_y': float, 'batsman_runs': integer]
# We have total_runs and total_runs_1 from source0 and source1 respectively
# The target has only one total_runs column (integer)
# We need to combine total_runs from source0 and source1 by summing them (sum aggregation)
# Also, batsman_runs_x and batsman_runs_y are float columns from source2 and source3 respectively
# The last column batsman_runs (integer) is presumably from source1 total_runs_1 or source0 total_runs? 
# The target examples show batsman_runs as integer, so likely sum of batsman_runs from source2 and source3 or total_runs_1?

# The target has batsman_runs_x (float), total_runs (int), batsman_runs_y (float), batsman_runs (int)
# So batsman_runs (int) likely sum of batsman_runs from source2 and source3 rounded or summed

# group by batsman
# mean of batsman_runs_x (from source2)

# mean of batsman_runs_y (from source3)
# sum of batsman_runs (from source2.batsman_runs + source3.batsman_runs rounded or cast to int)

# Let's create columns for aggregation accordingly

df_final["batsman_runs_sum"] = df_final["batsman_runs_x"] + df_final["batsman_runs_y"]

# Aggregate

    batsman_runs_x = ("batsman_runs_x", "mean"),
    total_runs = ("total_runs_sum", "sum"),
    batsman_runs_y = ("batsman_runs_y", "mean"),
    batsman_runs = ("batsman_runs_sum", "sum")

agg_df["batsman_runs"] = agg_df["batsman_runs"].astype(int)
